questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the challenges, / the team is determined to / completed / the project on time and within budget.

options.text: the project on time and within budget

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. completed .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the segment "**completed**".
 
• The verb "**completed**" is incorrect in this context because the sentence uses the phrase "**the team is determined to**", which requires the base form of the verb (infinitive without "to").
 
• The correct form should be "**complete**" instead of "**completed**".
 
• The correct structure is "**to + base form of the verb**", which aligns with the grammatical rule for verbs following "determined to".

Correct sentence: *Despite the challenges, the team is determined to **complete** the project on time and within budget.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common error in verb usage:**
 
 
• When a verb follows phrases like "**determined to**", "**want to**", or "**need to**", always use the base form of the verb.
 
• **Example:** She is determined to **win** the competition (not "winning" or "won").
 
 
 
• **How to identify such errors:**
 
 
• Look for auxiliary verbs like "**is**", "**was**", "**determined to**", and check if the following verb is in its correct base form.
 
 
</ul

• The word **"conspiracy"** refers to a secret plan made by a group of people to do something unlawful or harmful. (षड्यंत्र)

 
 
• **Example:** The authorities uncovered a conspiracy to overthrow the government.
 
 
 
• **"Plot"** is a synonym for conspiracy and means a secret plan or scheme, often with negative or harmful intentions. (साजिश)
 
 
• **Example:** They were arrested for plotting to sabotage the event.
 
 
 
• Thus, the word "plot" correctly conveys the meaning of "conspiracy" in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Plot**.

• **Example:** His motivation to succeed drove him to work harder than anyone else.

• **Example:** His willfulness often got him into trouble with his teachers.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**best**'.

__
 
• The adjective "**best**" is the superlative form of "**good**."
 
• The sentence requires a superlative form to indicate that Meera Narayan is the most suitable model for the advertisement.
 
• **Options 1, 2, and 3** are grammatically incorrect because they do not form valid superlative adjectives.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The **best**__ model who can be selected for this advertisement is Meera Narayan."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "more better"** is incorrect because "better" is already a comparative form, and adding "more" creates redundancy.
 
• **Option 2: "most best"** is incorrect because "best" is already a superlative form, and adding "most" creates redundancy.
 
• **Option 3: "most good"** is incorrect because "good" does not take "most" for forming its superlative; instead, it becomes "best."
